rows.jp: 桜庭に押し倒される夢を見た。
rows.en: I dreamed that Sakuraba pinned me down.

ghs.en: I dreamed of Sakuraba pushing himself on me.

rows.jp: 「……シュールすぎる」
rows.en: “...Way too surreal.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...way too surreal."

rows.jp: だいたいあいつに、人を押し倒す度胸なんてあるはずないのだ。
rows.en: For one thing, he would never have the nerve to pin anyone down.

ghs.en: Besides, I wouldn't expect that guy to have the pluck to push himself on somebody.

rows.jp: 朝食が用意してある。
rows.en: Breakfast was waiting for me.

rows.jp: メモもあった。
rows.en: There was a note, too.

rows.jp: 『しっかり食べて行ってらっしゃい』
rows.en: “Eat well. Have a good day.”

ghs.en: 『Eat properly and have a nice day』

rows.jp: 美人でキャリアな睦美おばさんは、料理もうまい。
rows.en: Aunt Mutsumi was beautiful, successful, and a good cook to boot.

ghs.en: Beautiful career woman Mutsumi-obasan is also good at cooking.

rows.jp: 忙しくて家にはほとんどいないけど。
rows.en: Though she was so busy she was almost never home.

ghs.en: She's so busy that she's almost never home, though.

rows.jp: 頭が下がる。
rows.en: I had to admire her.

ghs.en: I bow my head to that.

rows.jp: お言葉に甘えて、分厚いサンドイッチを野菜ジュースで流し込んだ。
rows.en: Taking her at her word, I washed down a thick sandwich with vegetable juice.

ghs.en: Presuming upon her kind offer, I wash down a thick sandwich with some vegetable juice.

rows.jp: 時間がない。
rows.en: I was running out of time.

ghs.en: I don't have time.

rows.jp: 残りはラップに包んでポケットに入れた。
rows.en: I wrapped up the rest and slipped it into my pocket.

rows.jp: 途中で食べていこう。
rows.en: I could eat it on the way.

rows.jp: しばらく歩いていると、
rows.en: After I’d been walking for a while—

rows.jp: 「あぎゃらおーーーーーーーーっ！！」
rows.en: “AGYAROOOOOOOOO!!”

rows.jp: 桜庭の悲鳴だ。
rows.en: That was Sakuraba screaming.

ghs.en: That's Sakuraba's scream.

rows.jp: わりと近い。
rows.en: Fairly close by.

ghs.en: It's relatively near.

rows.jp: 犬の吠え声と、悲鳴がさらに重なる。
rows.en: A dog’s barking joined the scream, then another scream piled on.

ghs.en: The howl of a dog further overlaps the scream.

rows.jp: 遠ざかっていく。
rows.en: The whole racket receded into the distance.

ghs.en: And then they fade away.

rows.jp: 「なるほど……」
rows.en: “I see...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I get it..."

rows.jp: 得心した。
rows.en: That explained it.

ghs.en: I was satisfied.

rows.jp: と、そこに―――
rows.en: And then—

ghs.en: Then, right there---

rows.jp: 「はれ？　太一さん？」
rows.en: “Huh? Taichi?”

ghs.en: Girl: "Oh my? Taichi-san?"

rows.jp: 「おはよう」
rows.en: “Morning.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "'Morning."

rows.jp: 「あ、おはようですっ」
rows.en: “Oh! Good morning!”

ghs.en: Girl: "Ah, good morning, yes!"

rows.jp: ぺこりと頭を下げる。
rows.en: She bowed her head.

ghs.en: She bows her head with a sharp bob.

rows.jp: 近所に住む美少女の遊紗ちゃん。
rows.en: Yusa, the beautiful girl who lived in my neighborhood.

ghs.en: This is Yusa-chan, the beautiful young girl that leaves near me.
ghs.assessment: The line identifies a beautiful girl who lives nearby. The English uses 'leaves' instead of 'lives,' reversing the residence verb through a mechanical word error.
ghs.remedy: Replace 'leaves' with 'lives.'

rows.jp: 上見坂いい街。
rows.en: Kamimisaka. What a town.

ghs.en: Nice town Kamisaka.

rows.jp: 説明不要なほど可愛い遊紗ちゃんの、両手にカレーパンが揺れていた。
rows.en: Yusa was cute beyond words, and curry bread swung from both hands.

ghs.en: Yusa-chan, so cute it doesn't require exposition, held a loaf of curry bread swaying in her hands.

rows.jp: 二人で並んで歩き出す。
rows.en: We set off side by side.

ghs.en: The two of us line up and set out to walk.

rows.jp: 別に今日にはじまったことでもない。
rows.en: Nothing unusual about that.

ghs.en: It's not really something that began today,

rows.jp: なにせ同じ学校に向かうのだから。
rows.en: We were heading to the same school, after all.

ghs.en: it's because the two of us are going towards the same school anyway.

rows.jp: 後ろから、『い゛っでら゛っしゃーい！！』というハスキーな声が聞こえた。
rows.en: From behind us came a husky cry of “HAAAAVE A GOOOOD DAAAY!”

ghs.en: From behind us I could hear a 『Habe a nice daaaaaaaay!』 in a husky voice.

rows.jp: 遊紗ちゃんの母君だ。
rows.en: Yusa’s august mother.

ghs.en: That is Yusa-chan's mother.

rows.jp: ちょっと重くていらっしゃる。
rows.en: She was a lady of some substance.

ghs.en: She's sort on the heavy side,
ghs.assessment: The intended euphemism that she is sort of on the heavy side is clear, but the missing 'of' creates a mechanical grammar error.
ghs.remedy: Use 'sort of on the heavy side.'

rows.jp: が、毎日楽しそうに生きておられるから、よしとしよう。
rows.en: But she seemed to enjoy every day of her life, so let’s call it good.

ghs.en: but it's all fine, since she lets me have something enjoyable every day.
ghs.assessment: The mother herself appears to live happily every day, which the narrator takes as sufficient. The English instead claims she provides him with daily enjoyment, changing the subject and inventing a benefit to him.
ghs.remedy: Say that she seems to enjoy life every day, so he will call it fine.

highlights.text: she lets me have something enjoyable every day

rows.jp: 平凡な家庭に生まれた美少女。
rows.en: A beautiful girl born to an ordinary family.

ghs.en: A beautiful girl that was born to a family this mediocre...

rows.jp: ただ一つ難点があるとすれば、世間を知らなすぎること。
rows.en: Her one shortcoming, if it could be called that, was knowing far too little of the world.

ghs.en: If I had to find a just one blemish in her, it'd be that she is completely clueless of all things worldly.
ghs.assessment: The duplicated determiner and adverb make a mechanical grammar error in an otherwise accurate statement that her one flaw is excessive naivety.
ghs.remedy: Use 'just one blemish' or 'a single blemish.'

rows.jp: そんな遊紗ちゃんの、異性の先輩として一番身近な俺に課せられた責任は小さくない。
rows.en: As the older male student Yusa knew best, I bore no small responsibility for guiding her.

ghs.en: As the most familiar Senpai of opposite sex to little Yusa-chan, the responsibility given me is no little thing.

rows.jp: 「いってきまーす！」
rows.en: “I’m off!”

ghs.en: Yusa: "I am going ooout!"

rows.jp: 手を振り返す、その顔に反抗期の陰もなく。
rows.en: She waved back, not a trace of adolescent rebellion on her face.

ghs.en: She returns a wave of the hand, on her face not a shadow of that rebellious age.

rows.jp: どころか、第一次性徴さえまだなのではないかと思われる節もある。
rows.en: There were even grounds to suspect she had yet to enter puberty.

ghs.en: Far from it, as it appears we're also at a time where even her primary sexual characteristics might not be there yet.

rows.jp: この真っ白なキャンバスを俺色に染めあげたいと思ってしまうのは男として至極当然のことだが中等コースの一年で身長は前から三番目で――
rows.en: For a man, wanting to stain that spotless canvas in his own colors was only natural—but she was a first-year in the middle-school division, third shortest in her class, and—

rows.jp: 憶えたての敬語がたどたどしくも初々しい遊紗ちゃんの純正は宝石にも増して煌びやかで我が妄想も汚すか否かの瀬戸際で――
rows.en: the shy, halting politeness Yusa had only just learned made her unspoiled innocence glitter brighter than any jewel, leaving my imagination swaying on the brink of whether to defile it, and—

rows.jp: いつも切なげかつ悩ましげに揺れているのであるがその反復思考自体すでにペド狂人のものであるという自覚はある。あるんだってば。
rows.en: swaying there so wistfully, so tantalizingly; and yes, I was aware that obsessively circling back to this already made me a deranged pedophile. I was aware, damn it.

rows.jp: ま、とにかく揺れているのだ。
rows.en: Anyway. It was still swaying.

ghs.en: Well, for now they're swaying.

rows.jp: そう、遊紗ちゃんが手に持つカレーパンの袋のように。
rows.en: The bags of curry bread in Yusa’s hands, that is.

ghs.en: Yes, just like that bag of curry bread that Yusa-chan has in her hands.

rows.jp: 「カレーパンだね」
rows.en: “Curry bread.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't that curry bread?"

rows.jp: 「です」
rows.en: “It is.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "It is!"

rows.jp: 歩くたびに前後にゆらゆら揺れる。
rows.en: They swayed back and forth with every step.

ghs.en: With each step a sway, back and forth, back and forth.

rows.jp: 両手を幽霊みたいに掲げて、誇示するかのように進む。
rows.en: She held both hands out like a ghost and walked along as though displaying her prizes.

ghs.en: As if being cradled by a ghost, the sway nothing but a manifestation of its existence.
ghs.assessment: She walks with both hands raised like a ghost, as if displaying the item. The English invents a ghost cradling something, changes the subject to the sway, and omits her pose and forward motion.
ghs.remedy: Say that she walks on with both hands raised like a ghost, as though showing it off.

highlights.text: As if being cradled by a ghost, the sway nothing but a manifestation of its existence.

rows.jp: 「それは……朝食？」
rows.en: “Is that... breakfast?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Is that... breakfast?"

rows.jp: 「あの、さっきそこに桜庭さんがいて」
rows.en: “Um, Sakuraba was just over there.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Uhm, Sakuraba-san was there earlier."

rows.jp: 「うん、いたね」
rows.en: “Yeah. He was.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yep, was is the word."

rows.jp: 「会いましたか？」
rows.en: “Did you see him?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Did you meet him?"

rows.jp: 「いや、形跡があった」
rows.en: “No. Just signs he’d been there.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "No, there was some evidence left."

rows.jp: 「けいせき？」
rows.en: “Evidence?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Evidence?"

rows.jp: 「ま、俺が来たときにはいなかったけど」
rows.en: “Well, he was gone by the time I got here.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Well, by the time I came around he wasn't among us anymore."

rows.jp: 「困っちゃいました」
rows.en: “I didn’t know what to do.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Oh, what a problem."

rows.jp: 「カレーパンあげようと思ったのですけど」
rows.en: “I wanted to give him some curry bread.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "I thought I would give him this curry bread."

rows.jp: 餌付けしようとしてたらしい。
rows.en: Apparently she had meant to tame him with food.

ghs.en: Seems like she was going to feed the wild animal to train it to human contact.

rows.jp: 「あいつ、コンバットに嫌われてるからさ」
rows.en: “Combat hates him.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's because Combat hates that guy."

rows.jp: 「吉田さんちの猛犬コンバットですね」
rows.en: “Combat, the vicious dog at the Yoshidas’ house.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "That ferocious dog Combat, at Yoshida-san's house?"

rows.jp: 「やつは凄いぞ。自力で鎖の繋がった楔を引き抜くことができる」
rows.en: “He’s incredible. He can pull the stake holding his chain right out of the ground.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "That guy's awesome. He can uproot the wedge where his chain is fastened on his own."

rows.jp: 「外出したい時に出ていき、戻りたい時に戻るのだ」
rows.en: “He goes out when he pleases and comes home when he pleases.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "When that guy wants to leave he leaves, when he wants to return he returns."

rows.jp: 「コンバットは一般のひとは攻撃しませんよ」
rows.en: “Combat doesn’t attack ordinary people.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "But Combat doesn't normally attack people!"
ghs.assessment: Doesn't normally attack people conveys a general rule with exceptions, but shifts the source's protected target class of ordinary people into a frequency claim.
ghs.remedy: Say that the dog does not attack ordinary members of the public.

rows.jp: 「本物の極道ってのはそういうものさ」
rows.en: “That’s how you know he’s a real gangster.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "And a true gangster is exactly that sort."

rows.jp: 「ごくどう……だったのか……」
rows.en: “So Combat... was a gangster...”

ghs.en: Yusa: "True... gangster...?"

rows.jp: 「今は恰幅が良くなってしまったが、奴には軍人の血が流れてるからな」
rows.en: “He’s gotten pretty stout these days, but the blood of a soldier still runs in his veins.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Today his physique has improved, but the blood of soldiers flows inside that guy."
ghs.assessment: The dog has now grown stout or portly, not improved its physique. The English reverses the bodily change into a positive fitness claim.
ghs.remedy: Use 'He's grown stout now, but...'

rows.jp: 「人間で言えば、戦争帰りの古き良き親分といったところか」
rows.en: “In human terms, he’s an old-school mob boss home from the war.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "To put it in human terms, I'd say he's sort of like a good ol' criminal boss having returned home from the war."

rows.jp: 「しかし桜庭にだけは攻撃をする」
rows.en: “But Sakuraba is the one person he attacks.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yet he only ever attacks Sakuraba."

rows.jp: 「不思議です」
rows.en: “How strange.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "That's inexplicable."

rows.jp: 「不思議だねぇ」
rows.en: “Very strange.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Inexplicable it is."

rows.jp: ゆったりとしたペースで歩く。
rows.en: We walked at an easy pace.

ghs.en: We walk at a leisurely pace.

rows.jp: 「これどうしたら……」
rows.en: “What should I do with these...?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "What will I do with this..."

rows.jp: 「おなか、すいてますか？」
rows.en: “Are you hungry?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Would you be hungry, maybe?"

rows.jp: 「一個ずつ食べようか？」
rows.en: “Want one each?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Wanna eat half each?"
ghs.assessment: He suggests eating one item each. The English instead divides a single item into halves, changing the quantity and action.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Want to eat one each?'

rows.jp: 「はい」
rows.en: “Yes.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Yes!"

rows.jp: 二人でカレーパンを食べた。
rows.en: We ate the curry bread together.

ghs.en: The two of us ate the curry bread.

rows.jp: 「ガッコー慣れた？」
rows.en: “Getting used to school?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "You fitting in at school?"

rows.jp: 「まだちょっと」
rows.en: “Not quite yet.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Well, a bit."

rows.jp: 「いじめは？」
rows.en: “Anyone bullying you?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Bullying?"

rows.jp: 「全然ないんです！　よかったですー！」
rows.en: “Not at all! I’m so glad!”

ghs.en: Yusa: "None there is none! I'm so lucky!"
ghs.assessment: The first clause correctly intends that there is none at all, but duplicates incompatible constructions and is mechanically ungrammatical.
ghs.remedy: Use 'There's none at all!'

rows.jp: 「だろうねぇ」
rows.en: “I thought not.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ain't that nice."
ghs.assessment: The reply conveys 'I thought so' or 'I figured,' confirming an expectation. The English changes this into a positive evaluation that the situation is nice.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Thought so' or 'I figured.'

rows.jp: 天下群青学院。群青上等である。
rows.en: Gunjo Academy, peerless under heaven. Gunjo reigned supreme.

ghs.en: Gunjou Institute the lone in the world. A first-rate Gunjou this is.

rows.jp: 「もし何かあったら、あたしには高等コースに知り合いがいっぱいいるんですますー、とか言って牽制してやりたまえ」
rows.en: “If anything happens, tell them, ‘I know lots of people in the senior division, yes-ma’am-sir!’ That ought to scare them off.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If anything bad happens, gladden me by feinting with something like, 'I know a looot of people in classes above that will payback you!'."
ghs.assessment: He advises her to deter trouble by saying she knows many people in the upper course, with a joking imitation of her speech. The English invents pleasing him and a promise of retaliation, while 'feinting' does not express warning others off.
ghs.remedy: Tell her to hold them in check by saying she knows lots of people in the upper course, retaining the playful speech imitation.

highlights.text: gladden me by feinting with something like, 'I know a looot of people in classes above that will payback you!'

rows.jp: 「はい」
rows.en: “Yes.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Yes!"

rows.jp: 超嬉しそう。
rows.en: She looked absolutely delighted.

ghs.en: She looks hyper happy.

rows.jp: 「もう、ですます、とか言いませんけど……」
rows.en: She looked absolutely thrilled.

ghs.en: Yusa: "But really, I don't say things like 'will payback you'..."
ghs.assessment: She says she no longer uses the childish hybrid polite ending being teased. The English instead repeats an invented threat from the prior mistranslation and entirely omits the speech-habit correction.
ghs.remedy: Say that she does not say 'desu-masu' like that anymore, with enough context to preserve the teased speech habit.

rows.jp: 照れる。
rows.en: She blushed.

ghs.en: Shyness.

rows.jp: 「はっはっは」
rows.en: “Ha ha ha.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hah hah hah!"

rows.jp: 昔ちょっとからかったのを根に持ってるな。
rows.en: So she still held a grudge over my teasing her about it.

ghs.en: There's this resentfulness due to having been bullied some time ago.
ghs.assessment: She still holds a grudge because the narrator teased her a little in the past. The English makes her the passive victim of unspecified bullying and intensifies the action.
ghs.remedy: Say that she still resents him for teasing her a little before.

rows.jp: 「担任は榊原先生だっけ？」
rows.en: “Mr. Sakakibara is your homeroom teacher, right?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Homeroom teacher's Sakakibara-sensei, right?"

rows.jp: 「はい」
rows.en: “Yes.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Yes."

rows.jp: 「いい先生だよ。君はついてる」
rows.en: “He’s a good teacher. You got lucky.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "He's a good teacher! You're in luck."

rows.jp: 趣味は美少女フィギュアとちょっと終わりかけだが。
rows.en: Though his hobby of collecting pretty-girl figures put him dangerously close to being a lost cause.

ghs.en: Hobby's Bishoujo Figurines so he's sorta near the end, tho.
ghs.assessment: The narrator jokes that the teacher is a little far gone or hopeless because his hobby is beautiful-girl figures. 'Near the end' literalizes the idiom without conveying that judgment.
ghs.remedy: Use 'though his bishoujo-figure hobby means he's a little far gone.'

rows.jp: 「あはあは、どーも」
rows.en: “Ahaha. Thank you.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Ahah ahah, thanks!"

rows.jp: 「……クラスのみんなも一生懸命生きてて、わたし楽しいです」
rows.en: “...Everyone in my class is trying their very best to live. I’m having fun.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "...everybody in my class gives it all they have, so they can have fun with me!"
ghs.assessment: She says that everyone in class is living or trying their hardest and that she herself is having fun. The English makes their effort serve the purpose of letting them have fun with her.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Everyone in class is trying their best, and I'm having fun.'

highlights.text: so they can have fun with me

rows.jp: 「そっか」
rows.en: “I see.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Do they now."

rows.jp: 「おかーさんもいてくれるし」
rows.en: “And my mom is here with me.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Mommy's also always trying to help me."

rows.jp: 「だな」
rows.en: “True.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Isn't she."

rows.jp: 「いざとなったらあの人が出張るか。いや遊紗ちゃん、きみの生活安泰だ」
rows.en: “And if anything did happen, your mother would charge right in. Yusa, you’ve got it made.”

ghs.en: Taichi: Ah, but when things get tough that woman truly stands out. Well, Yusa-chan, yours is a life of peace!"
ghs.assessment: He says that in a crisis her mother will step in or take the field. 'Stands out' describes prominence rather than intervention and loses the protective contingency.
ghs.remedy: Use 'when things get tough, that woman will step in.'

rows.jp: 「それと……あの……」

ghs.en: Yusa: "And then... uhm..."

rows.en: “Hm?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Hm?"

rows.jp: 「先生が、交換日記しろって」
rows.en: “Our teacher told us to keep an exchange diary.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "The teacher had us do exchange diaries..."

rows.jp: 「そんな授業あったなあ、昔」
rows.en: “We had an assignment like that once.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I had that too class too, long ago."
ghs.assessment: The line recalls having that class long ago, but two competing placements of 'too' remain in the sentence and create a mechanical grammar error.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I had that class too, long ago.'

rows.jp: 交流ＨＲだっけ。
rows.en: Was that called Exchange Homeroom?

ghs.en: Homeroom Exchange, was it.

rows.jp: 「俺、クラスであぶれちゃってさ、高等コースの人とやったよ」
rows.en: “I was left without a partner in my class, so they paired me with someone in the senior division.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Me, I didn't really find anyone in my class, so I did it with someone from a higher grade."

rows.jp: 「あ、わたしもあぶれました」
rows.en: “Oh. I was left without a partner too.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Ah, I did not find anyone either!"

rows.en: “Huh?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eh?"

rows.jp: 「うち、奇数なんで」
rows.en: “There’s an odd number of us.”

ghs.en: Yusa: "We are an odd number in class."

rows.jp: 「ああ……じゃ先生と？」
rows.en: “Oh... So you’re keeping one with your teacher?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ahhh... so, how about the teacher?"
ghs.assessment: He infers that she therefore paired with the teacher. The English makes the teacher a new suggestion rather than a question about what already happened.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Ah... so, with the teacher?'

rows.jp: 「いえ、あの、それでです」
rows.en: “No. Um... that’s why...”

ghs.en: Yusa: "No, see, it is this here."

rows.jp: 鞄の中から、ごそごそとノートを取り出す。
rows.en: She rummaged through her bag and brought out a notebook.

ghs.en: With a rustling, she takes out a notebook from inside her bag.

rows.jp: 「太一さんに、お願いできませんか？」
rows.en: “Would you do it with me, Taichi?”

ghs.en: Yusa: "Taichi-san, couldn't I entrust you with this?"

rows.jp: カラフルグリーンのノート。
rows.en: A notebook in a vivid, cheerful green.

ghs.en: A neon-green notebook,

rows.jp: ほのかにミントの香り。
rows.en: It carried a faint scent of mint.

ghs.en: a faint scent of mint.

rows.jp: 「よし、やろう！」
rows.en: “All right! Let’s do it!”

ghs.remedy: Use 'The girl's gaze rested steadily on my white hair.'

rows.jp: 気がつくと、よく顔やら髪やらを見られている。

ghs.en: Now that I think of it, there was once a prince that appeared in a Co**lt novel that I'm sure was handsome despite his snow-white hair.
ghs.assessment: The remembered prince is a handsome white-haired man; the hair is part of the description. 'Despite' invents a concession that treats the white hair as an obstacle to his beauty.
ghs.remedy: Say that the prince was a handsome man with white hair.

rows.jp: 熱く語っていた。
rows.en: She had talked about him with tremendous enthusiasm.

ghs.en: So much passion around that one.
ghs.assessment: The source says that she had spoken passionately about the prince. The nominal English mentions ambient passion but omits both the speaker and the act of telling him.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She'd talked passionately about him.'

highlights.text: So much passion around that one.

rows.jp: してみると俺は、王子様とイメージしているのだろうか。

ghs.en: Well then, I should have that same princely image myself, right?
ghs.assessment: He wonders whether she therefore imagines him as a prince. The English makes the princely image something he himself should possess and removes her as the perceiving subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Does that mean she imagines me as a prince?'

highlights.text: I should have that same princely image myself

ghs.assessment: The German address is emitted with literal brace markup in the middle of the word, producing a visible typography defect rather than the intended form.
ghs.remedy: Render the address as 'Fräulein' or a consistent plain-ASCII equivalent.
